bridge_requirements_named_by_leg_348.what_the_bridge_needs: Every located periodic-orbit/branch CAP closure (leg 348 sec.3-4) closes its tail-domination (neglected-mode) estimate against a COMPACT domain (torus, bounded box with Dirichlet/Navier BC, minimal periodic cell) using a discrete, geometrically/exponentially decaying spectral basis (Fourier or Chebyshev). Route 4's object needs the same KIND of closure -- a rigorous, two-sided, computable bound on the norm of the truncated tail of the basis expansion -- but on an UNBOUNDED R^3 domain, in an algebraically weighted space, for a vector-valued (Leray-projected) Navier-Stokes state.
four_named_asks_a_candidate_basis_must_m: (i) DIMENSION: genuinely R^3 (or a validated tensor-product/radial reduction of it), not 1D or a single radial coordinate alone
(ii) STATE SPACE: vector-valued, divergence-free / Leray-projected Navier-Stokes fields, not a scalar model equation
(iii) RIGOR GRADE: a validated / two-sided / interval-arithmetic-usable tail bound (CAP-grade), not an asymptotic numerical-analysis convergence-rate estimate

(iv) DECAY OF THE TAIL BOUND ITSELF: geometric or exponential in the truncation order, so that a finite Galerkin cutoff plus a rigorously bounded remainder actually closes at finite computational cost -- algebraic weight, per leg 260's own sharp threshold (s>1, p>3), caps how fast a coefficient sequence for a function IN that space can decay, an internal risk factor flagged (not proved) by leg 334 sec.3.3 for a different but related operator

published_tail_completeness_result.citation: J. P. Boyd, "The Rate of Convergence of Hermite Function Series", Mathematics of Computation 35(152), 1980, pp. 1309-1316.
published_tail_completeness_result.quote_or_paraphrase: Snippet-level read (not full text): convergence rate of a Hermite series depends not only on the order p of an entire function (or the location of the nearest singularity for a singular function, as in ordinary power series) but ALSO on the parameter 'a', the exponent of the function's real-axis decay -- i.e. coefficient decay is governed jointly by analyticity and by how fast the target itself decays on the real line, not by analyticity alone.
published_tail_completeness_result.completeness: Standard result (textbook, e.g. Boyd's 'Chebyshev and Fourier Spectral Methods'; not separately re-derived here): Hermite functions are a complete orthonormal basis of L^2(R). Multi-D completeness in L^2(R^3) follows by the usual tensor-product argument for the scalar case; not itself the object route 4 needs (vector-valued, weighted, not L^2 with Gaussian weight).

per_basis_table.gap_against_bridge: Fails (iv) directly and by construction: the Gaussian weight is EXACTLY the one weight family leg 260/341 excluded from route 4's function space (leg 260 sec.1: the object's own |y|^{-1}-type Type-I decay does not sit in a Gaussian-weighted space at all -- it sits outside it, the same way it sits outside L^3). A basis whose completeness is proved in the excluded space is not a candidate; it is cited here only as the baseline against which the algebraic-weight variants below are contrasted.
per_basis_table.read_at: abstract/snippet level only (search-engine excerpts of the AMS/JSTOR listing), consistent with leg 348's own disclosed practice of not fetching full text where the load-bearing quote is visible at abstract/snippet resolution

citations: X. M. Xiang, Z. Q. Wang, "Generalized Hermite Spectral Method and its Applications to Problems in Unbounded Domains", SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 48(4), 2010, pp. 1231-1253.
C. Zhang, B.-Y. Guo, "Generalized Hermite spectral method matching asymptotic behaviors", Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 255, 2014, pp. 616-634.
B.-Y. Guo, C. Zhang, "Generalized Hermite Spectral Method Matching Different Algebraic Decay at Infinities", Journal of Scientific Computing 65(2), 2015, pp. 648-671.
B.-Y. Guo, "Error estimation of Hermite spectral method for nonlinear partial differential equations", Mathematics of Computation 68(227), 1999, pp. 1067-1078.
published_tail_completeness_result.quote_or_paraphrase: Snippet-level read: Zhang-Guo (2014) construct generalized Hermite functions mutually orthogonal with respect to the ALGEBRAIC weight (1+x^2)^{-gamma} for real gamma, and establish orthogonal-approximation results explicitly tied to the asymptotic (algebraic) decay rate of the approximated function; Guo-Zhang (2015) extends this to functions with DIFFERENT algebraic decay rates at the two ends of the line. These are the closest-matching published results to route 4's own algebraic weight family located this leg.
published_tail_completeness_result.completeness: Weighted-Sobolev-space error estimates are proved (per the paraphrase above), not merely completeness -- this is a stronger and more directly useful published result than a bare completeness theorem, when it applies.

per_basis_table.gap_against_bridge: Fails (i): every located paper in this family is 1D (a scalar function on the real line), with no located published extension to R^3 or to vector/Leray-projected fields. Fails (iii): these are numerical-analysis ERROR-RATE papers (asymptotic-in-N approximation-order results), not validated/interval CAP papers with a rigorously bounded two-sided tail -- none of the abstracts read this leg claim a computer-assisted-proof-grade enclosure. Ambiguous on (iv): an algebraic weight bounding the target's own decay generally yields an ALGEBRAIC (not geometric/exponential) rate of coefficient decay for that same weight class, per the Boyd (1980) dependence-on-'a' result above and consistent with leg 334 sec.3.3's internal continuous-spectrum flag -- if so, a Galerkin truncation under this basis pays a POLYNOMIAL-in-N tail bound rather than the exponential one every located compact-domain CAP closure (leg 348) actually uses, which is a structural mismatch with the bridge's own working method, not merely an unproven gap. This is the single most decision-relevant row in the table: it is the closest match on WEIGHT but the furthest matched-in-published-form from the bridge's own operating regime.
per_basis_table.read_at: search-engine snippet/abstract level only; no PDF or LaTeX fetched this leg. Full-text reading (in particular, checking whether Zhang-Guo/Guo-Zhang state the coefficient-decay rate as algebraic vs. geometric explicitly, rather than this leg inferring it from Boyd (1980) and leg 334's internal flag) is named below as the cheapest concrete next step if the user authorizes further scoping short of cost class C.

per_basis_table.basis: Rational Chebyshev functions on a semi-infinite/infinite interval (Boyd's TL_n / TB_n maps)

citations: J. P. Boyd, "Orthogonal Rational Functions on a Semi-infinite Interval", Journal of Computational Physics 70, 1987, pp. 63-88.

J. P. Boyd, "The Optimization of Convergence for Chebyshev Polynomial Methods in an Unbounded Domain", Journal of Computational Physics 45, 1982, pp. 43-79 (located by title/author search this leg; not independently abstract-read -- carried at citation level only, flagged as such).
C. I. Christov, "A Complete Orthonormal System of Functions in L^2(-infinity,infinity) Space", SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics 42(6), 1982, pp. 1337-1344.
published_tail_completeness_result.quote_or_paraphrase: Boyd (1987) abstract, snippet-level: introduces the rational Chebyshev functions TL_n(y) on the semi-infinite interval via a mapping of standard Chebyshev polynomials, stated (in the truncated snippet retrieved) to retain 'orthogonality, completeness, exponential o[r algebraic convergence]' (fragment cut off in the available excerpt; the completeness claim itself is legible, the convergence-rate clause is not fully legible and is NOT quoted further than this). Christov (1982) proves a distinct but related rational-Chebyshev-type system is a complete orthonormal system of L^2(R) -- a genuine completeness theorem, in the unweighted L^2 case.
published_tail_completeness_result.completeness: Completeness in (unweighted or Gaussian-analogue-weighted) L^2 on the semi-infinite or infinite line is published and load-bearing (Christov 1982; Boyd 1987). This is this leg's most solidly SOURCED completeness result of the three genuinely spectral (non-Boyd-map-composite) candidates.

per_basis_table.gap_against_bridge: Fails (i): 1D again, no located R^3 extension. Fails/underdetermined on (iv): this leg's own snippet-level read of Boyd (1987) could not confirm the exact convergence-rate clause (the fragment was truncated mid-sentence: 'exponential o[r]...'), so whether TL_n/TB_n achieve exponential convergence for algebraically-decaying targets, or only algebraic convergence matched to the target's own decay order (the standard Boyd-map behaviour: convergence is geometric in the MAPPED variable only for targets that are themselves analytic in a Bernstein-type region after mapping, and degrades to algebraic for targets with only algebraic decay) is RECORDED AS UNCONFIRMED BY THIS LEG'S OWN READING, not asserted either way. This is a genuine literature-read gap, disclosed rather than papered over. Fails (iii): none of the three located papers is a validated/CAP-grade result; they are classical numerical-analysis convergence papers from the 1980s, predating the validated-numerics literature this repository otherwise draws on.
per_basis_table.read_at: search-engine snippet/abstract level only for Boyd (1987) and Christov (1982); Boyd (1982) located by citation search only (title/author/journal/pages), its own abstract NOT read this leg -- flagged explicitly as the weakest-sourced citation in this table, carried only because it is the standard citation for the rational-Chebyshev optimization-of-convergence result and its omission would understate the row's literature base, not because this leg verified its content.

per_basis_table.basis: Mapped Laguerre functions (algebraic or exponential map to a half-line)

citations: O. Coulaud, D. Funaro, O. Kavian, "Laguerre Spectral Approximation of Elliptic Problems in Exterior Domains", Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 80(1-3), 1990, pp. 451-458, DOI 10.1016/0045-7825(90)90050-V.
published_tail_completeness_result.quote_or_paraphrase: Snippet-level read: the paper applies a Laguerre-function basis directly on an exterior (unbounded) domain, contrasted in the retrieved snippet with an alternative (Guo's) approach that instead maps the unbounded problem onto a bounded domain first -- i.e. Coulaud-Funaro-Kavian is presented as the DIRECT-basis-on-the-unbounded-domain line, distinct from the map-then-Chebyshev line the other two rows use.
published_tail_completeness_result.completeness: Not independently confirmed by this leg's read (the retrieved snippet did not state a completeness theorem in citable form); Laguerre functions' completeness in L^2(0,infinity) with the standard exponential weight is well-known textbook material (e.g. Boyd's spectral-methods text, cited but not independently re-derived) -- flagged as carried-not-verified for the algebraic-weight variant specifically.

per_basis_table.gap_against_bridge: This is the weakest-sourced row in the table, disclosed as such per the gate's own instruction that an underdetermined row is itself decision-relevant information. This leg located exactly one paper (Coulaud-Funaro-Kavian 1990) applying Laguerre bases to unbounded/exterior-domain elliptic problems, and could NOT confirm from the retrieved snippet whether it addresses algebraic weights specifically, general elliptic problems, or specific convergence rates -- the search returned only a citation and one contrastive sentence, not a quotable theorem statement. No published Laguerre-family result matching route 4's specific algebraic weight rho=(1+|y|)^{-s}, s>1 was located this leg. Fails (i)/(ii)/(iii) for the same structural reasons as the other 1D scalar rows, and additionally fails to clear even the basic literature-location bar the other rows cleared.
per_basis_table.read_at: citation-level only; one contrastive sentence from a search-engine snippet, no abstract fetched, no PDF fetched. This is recorded as a genuine literature gap in THIS LEG's own search, not a claim that no such literature exists -- the repository's own MF1/MF4 discipline (leg 348 sec.1-2) requires distinguishing 'not found by this leg's queries' from 'does not exist', and this row is the clearest instance of the former in this table.

per_basis_table.basis: Boyd-map composite families in general, including leg 350's own log-Boyd composition (log map removing an endpoint branch point, then a fixed algebraic Boyd map u/(u+L), Chebyshev-in-mapped-variable)

published_tail_completeness_result.citation: Leg 350's own construction is INTERNAL to this repository (experiments/journal/leg_350.md sections 2-4; solver/dssp_basis.py), not itself a published external result. Its underlying TECHNIQUE (log-map to remove a branch-point singularity, algebraic map to compactify the resulting semi-infinite variable) is textbook (J. P. Boyd, Chebyshev and Fourier Spectral Methods, 2nd ed., 2001 -- general reference, not independently re-read this leg beyond leg 350's own citation of it) but the SPECIFIC composition applied to a DSS/log-periodic far-field target was checked for prior art by leg 350's own novelty pass and found ABSENT from arXiv title/abstract search (writeup/novelty/leg_350.md: five controlled queries, all zero except one off-topic hit), a controlled absence leg 350 itself reads as expected and uninformative (the general technique is decades old and not scoped to Navier-Stokes), not as a discovery.
published_tail_completeness_result.quote_or_paraphrase: Leg 350's own measured result: on this repository's specific boundary-block target function (1-X)^{1-i*kappa}, the log-Boyd composite basis resolves the target at 25.7x-28.5x fewer modes than plain Chebyshev, at identical 1e-6 truncation, with two controls (kappa=0, and a smooth function with no boundary singularity) each showing the map is NOT a universal compressor -- a real, falsifiable, NEW NUMBER on a repository-internal target, per leg 350's own framing, not a new numerical-analysis technique and not a completeness or convergence-rate THEOREM of any generality.
published_tail_completeness_result.completeness: Not established, not attempted, and not claimed by leg 350 -- leg 350's gate was a mode-count comparison on one specific scalar boundary-block function, not a basis-completeness or tail-bound proof.

per_basis_table.gap_against_bridge: This is the UNINVENTORIABLE row named by the gate's own branch: the literature genuinely underdetermines it. There is no published tail/completeness theorem for THIS composite map family at all (it is this repository's own internal instrument, built and measured by leg 350 for a single scalar target, not sourced to external literature beyond the generic textbook technique). It therefore cannot be scored against the bridge's four asks in the same sourced way the other rows were: (i)-(iv) are each simply UNANSWERED by any citable external result, and leg 350's own internal 1e-6-truncation mode-count measurement is not a rigorous/validated tail bound in the CAP sense the bridge needs (fails (iii) by leg 350's own admission -- 'CEILING: TIER 2 unchanged... not a certificate'). Recorded as itself decision-relevant: if cost-class-C spend were to start from the basis MOST ALREADY FAMILIAR to this repository's own tooling, this is it, but 'most familiar' and 'closest to a published tail bound' are not the same axis, and this row scores highest on the former and lowest (tied with mapped Laguerre) on the latter.

cross_row_finding.headline: No row in this table publishes a result meeting all four of the bridge's named asks (R^3, vector/Leray-projected, CAP-grade validated tail bound, geometric-in-truncation decay) simultaneously. Every genuinely spectral candidate (Hermite-family, rational-Chebyshev-family, Laguerre-family) is 1D/scalar in its published form; the one basis this repository has actually built and measured against an algebraic-weight-adjacent target (leg 350's log-Boyd composition) is an internal instrument on a single scalar function, not a sourced external completeness/tail result, and is explicitly NOT a certificate by its own leg's account.
cross_row_finding.closest_match_on_weight: Generalized Hermite functions with algebraic weight (1+x^2)^{-gamma} (Xiang-Wang 2010 / Zhang-Guo 2014 / Guo-Zhang 2015) -- closest published match to route 4's own algebraic-weight family, but with an unresolved and structurally suggestive concern (per Boyd 1980's dependence on the real-axis decay exponent 'a', and leg 334 sec.3.3's internal continuous-spectrum flag for a related operator) that the coefficient-decay rate achievable under an algebraic weight may itself be algebraic rather than geometric -- which, if it holds, would mean this basis family does not supply the KIND of tail bound (exponential-in-truncation) every located compact-domain CAP closure (leg 348) actually relies on, independent of the R^3/vector-field gap every row shares.
cross_row_finding.least_sourced_row: Mapped Laguerre functions -- this leg located exactly one paper (Coulaud-Funaro-Kavian 1990) and could not extract a citable theorem statement from the available snippet; recorded per the gate's own instruction as itself decision-relevant (an unresolved literature gap, not a failure of this leg to search).
cross_row_finding.what_cost_class_C_would_have_to_buy_firs: Per this inventory alone (no construction attempted, no recommendation to build endorsed by this leg): the two cheapest-looking literature gaps to close BEFORE any basis-construction work would be (a) a full-text read of Zhang-Guo (2014) / Guo-Zhang (2015) to settle whether their generalized-Hermite coefficient-decay estimate is stated as algebraic or geometric in truncation order -- this is a reading task, not a construction task, and could resolve the table's single most decision-relevant open question without entering cost class C; and (b) determining whether any published extension of ANY row to R^3 vector fields (not scalar 1D) exists via a more targeted search than this leg ran (this leg's own arXiv-API queries were not re-run for this table; the citations above were located by general web/citation search, a different instrument than leg 348/350's arXiv-API novelty passes, and cross-checking with the arXiv-API instrument is a cheap next step, not itself cost-class C). Both are literature-reading tasks. This leg does not recommend, size, or schedule either -- that determination belongs to the user's ruling, per the gate's own scope.
